page: Microsoft Azure D16plds_v6 is an ARM64-based virtual machine configured with 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs powered by the Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. Hyper-threading is absent, offering a strict 1:1 mapping between vCPUs and physical cores. Memory capacity is provisioned at 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. For high-speed temporary workloads, the instance includes 944 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The processor carries a 128 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 64 KB L1d cache, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration for AES.

Benchmark outcomes show competitive throughput in memory-bound scenarios. Uncached large-block read bandwidth reaches 307.54 GB/sec and write bandwidth achieves 124.58 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25 percent tier alongside a strong PassMark memory score of 2,945.61. CPU processing across standard multi-threaded suites—including Geekbench multi-core (14,736.0), Geekbench software compilation (25,142.0), and stress-ng multi-core (33,160.55)—consistently lands in the middle 50 percent range. In data handling, single-threaded gzip compression achieves strong performance at 33.08 GB/sec.

Without hardware GPU acceleration, the system handles lightweight inference adequately for small models, producing 263.31 tokens per second on text generation using a 135M model. However, medium models (7B) reveal hardware limitations, dropping prompt processing into the lower 25 percent tier at 24.62 tokens per second.

Given its compute-heavy 1:2 core-to-memory allocation, high uncached memory bandwidth, and integrated 944 GB local NVMe storage, Microsoft Azure D16plds_v6 provides balanced efficiency for compute-centric, I/O-intensive workloads. It is well aligned with CI/CD build pipelines, code compilation, web serving, decompression pipelines, and distributed data processing nodes where memory density requirements remain under 2 GB per core.
description: Microsoft Azure D16plds_v6 is an ARM-based compute instance built on the 3.4 GHz Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 architecture, featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped directly to 16 physical cores. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of RAM (a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio), 944 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and no GPU hardware. Benchmark results display strong uncached memory bandwidth, achieving 307.54 GB/sec on reads and 124.58 GB/sec on writes, alongside upper-quartile gzip compression throughput. Core processing tests such as Geekbench multi-core (14,736.0) and stress-ng remain in the middle 50 percent range. While larger AI inference workloads are constrained by memory and lack of acceleration, the bundled NVMe disk and high multi-core throughput make this instance suitable for build farms, CI/CD pipelines, web serving, and distributed compute workloads requiring low per-core memory footprints.
